issues.failure_explanation: The velocity energy bound is linear in \|\mathbf f\|_{\mathbf H^{-1}}, but the pressure recovered through the inf-sup identity also contains the convective term b(y;y,\cdot), which the paper's own trilinear estimate bounds only quadratically in \|\nabla y\|_2. Thus the stated pressure bound for every f\in H^{-1} is stronger than the supported estimate; without a data bound one only gets a bound of the form \|p\|_2\lesssim \|\mathbf f\|_{H^{-1}}+\|\mathbf f\|_{H^{-1}}^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the estimate to a bounded subset of H^{-1}(\Omega) data, e.g. admissible controls, or replace it by \|\nabla y\|_2+\|p\|_2\lesssim \|\mathbf f\|_{H^{-1}}+\|\mathbf f\|_{H^{-1}}^2.
issues.overall_effect: Only the general preliminary pressure estimate is unreliable for unbounded data. Later uses involve controls in the bounded admissible set, so the needed uniform bounds there survive after correction.
issues.title: Linear pressure a priori bound is stated for arbitrary H^{-1} data
issues.why_classification: The correction is local to the preliminary a priori estimate and preserves every later use, since the paper's data are uniformly bounded in L^\infty; no rate, method, or advertised regime changes.

issues.failure_explanation: J is defined as an infimum over the whole solution set S(u), while Theorem thm:properties_C_to_S gives only a local implicit branch and uniqueness in a neighborhood of (\bar y,\bar p). Regularity of \bar y does not imply S(u)=\{\mathcal S(u)\} for nearby controls, nor that the regular branch attains the infimum defining J. Hence J need not equal the smooth branch cost on U_ad\cap\mathcal O(\bar u), and the stated C^2 property and derivative formulas for J are not a direct consequence of the cited theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the minimized functional coincide with the differentiated branch: explicitly assume global state selection on the relevant control neighborhood, i.e. S(u)=\{\mathcal S(u)\} and J(u)=\frac12\|\mathcal S(u)_1-y_\Omega\|_2^2 for u\in U_ad\cap\mathcal O(\bar u), or else reformulate the problem as optimization over the local state-control branch and change the definition of local solution accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The derivative formulas for J, the displayed first-order necessary condition, the meaning of the growth assumption, and the quantitative local-optimality and error-estimate chain built from Taylor expansions of J are unreliable for the problem as defined.
issues.title: Differentiability of the reduced cost uses global uniqueness that regularity does not give
issues.why_classification: Regularity gives only local uniqueness; the needed global state selection is an additional Navier-Stokes uniqueness assumption or a change of the optimization problem. Either supported resolution removes the multiple-state situation that the paper explicitly allows or changes the central object, so a comparable result for the stated reduced problem is not preserved.
